chunks: Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from one of them عليهما السلام, who said:

"Indeed, the most severe matter that people will face on the Day of Resurrection is that the صاحب of khums will stand and say: 'My Lord, my khums.' And we have made that lawful for our Shi'ah so that their births may be pure, or so that their births may be purified."

key_terms.الْخُمُسِ: khums, the one-fifth due designated as a financial right
key_terms.شِيعَتِنَا: our Shi'ah, the followers of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.وِلَادَتُهُمْ: their birth or offspring, referring to purity of lineage
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection, when ultimate claims and accountability are established

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe khums and its effect on the purity of the Shi'ah's offspring?
ai.summary: This hadith states that claims concerning khums are among the grave matters that arise on the Day of Resurrection. It also reports that the Imams عليهم السلام made this right permissible for their Shi'ah so that the purity of their offspring and birth would be safeguarded.
